blind.description: A stylized rustic wooden shoring or mine support frame consisting of two upright timber posts, a jointed horizontal crossbeam held together with wooden collar bands and square pegs, and an interior diagonal brace supporting the center. A small wooden wedge or peg projects outwards near the base of one upright. Surfaces are solid, stylized low-poly geometry with hand-painted dark brown wood grain textures and warm edge highlights. It stands directly on its post bases without an added plinth.
blind.from_above: Seen from straight above, it appears as a thick wooden beam structure slightly kinked at the center joint, bounded by square collars/pegs at both ends, with a small wooden foot wedge protruding to one side.
blind.height_vs_figure: About 4.5 to 5 feet tall (standing roughly shoulder-height to the 5 ft 9 in scale figure) and roughly 3.5 to 4 feet wide.
